newsitem.title: USA: Telmex, Telebras ADRs hit yr highs.
newsitem.headline: Telmex, Telebras ADRs hit yr highs.

text.p: Latin American telecommunications companies Telefonos de Mexico and Telebras hit 12-month highs on Wednesday, pulled higher in part by a record-breaking Dow, analysts said.
Telefonos de Mexico, or Telmex, closed up 1-3/4 to 40-3/4 and Telebras, Brazil's telecommunications holding, rose 3-3/4 to close at 93-7/8.
Telmex was the New York Stock Exchange's volume leader with 5.6 million shares traded and Telebras also was among the top 25 most-active stocks.

Rizwan Ali, a telecommunications analyst at Bear Stearns, said the rise in Telmex and Telebras was in part caused by the strong performance of the New York markets. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed on Wednesday unofficially at a record 6961.63.

"There is no fundamental reason for Telmex to be up this much. I give it another couple of weeks to correct," he said, noting that the former monopoly had reported disappointing 1996 results this week.
Telmex also was helped by lower Mexican interest rates, which spurred the Mexican stock exchange to a record close.

Ali and Ana Wong, a trader in Brazilian shares at UBS Securities, said Telebras was being boosted by strong prospects for privatization and steps to let Brazil's reformist president run for re-election.

"Telebras is the cheapest stock in Latin America in the (telecommunications) sector" in terms of valuation, Wong said. "I think there is a lot of flow from people that think the U.S. is too expensive and they want to diversify to international" stocks.

Among other telecommunications stocks, Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile closed up 3/4 at a year high of 28, helped by lower interest rates in Chile, and Venezuela's CANTV rose one to close at 29-3/4, also a high since its November New York debut.
